name: Gornergletscher

tier.2016: interpolated between the 2015 survey, the 2021/2022 lidar and the 2023 survey (GLAMOS-style lowering shape); not checked (no summer ICESat-2 shots)

tier.2019: interpolated between the 2015 survey, the 2021/2022 lidar and the 2023 survey (GLAMOS-style lowering shape); not checked (no summer ICESat-2 shots)
tier.2020: interpolated between the 2015 survey, the 2021/2022 lidar and the 2023 survey (GLAMOS-style lowering shape); checked against ICESat-2: 215 shots, rmse 1.92 m
tier.2021: interpolated; the swissSURFACE3D lidar flown 2021-08-26 sits on 48 % of the ice cells (computed) and fixes them; checked against ICESat-2: 287 shots, rmse 1.38 m
tier.2022: interpolated; the swissSURFACE3D lidar flown 2022-08-23 sits on 41 % of the ice cells (computed) and fixes them; checked against ICESat-2: 319 shots, rmse 1.88 m
tier.2023: measured: newest swissALTI3D edition (2024 edition, aerial images 2023), placed at 2023-08-21 (a real strip day, the one that fits ICESat-2 best); checked against ICESat-2: 513 shots, rmse 1.74 m

tier.2025: extrapolated beyond the 2023 survey at the cell scale of the last segment, from the smoothed difference of the surveys; checked against ICESat-2: 443 shots, rmse 2.43 m

summary: Ice surface of each year 2016 to 2026 on the 3D strip: two swisstopo elevation models (2015, 2023), swisstopo lidar on part of the tongue (2021, 2022) and an elevation-band lowering shape for the years between and beyond. A model, not a measurement, except where a survey lies.

anchors.survey: GLAMOS volume-change table (release 2025) lists this surface as source "sa3d-2018" with date_end 20159999: survey 2015, day unknown. Image strips over the whole strip in 2015 (swisstopo layer ch.swisstopo.lubis-bildstreifen): 2015-08-26 (TLM, 0.5 m, covers every ice cell), 2015-08-05 (CRYOSPHERE MONITORING, 74 % of ice cells, computed), 2015-09-20 (TLM, 58 % of ice cells, computed). Which strip fed which cell is not published.
anchors.placed_at: 2015-08-26 (assumption: the strip that covers all ice cells)

anchors.source: swissSURFACE3D raster (swisstopo lidar DSM, 0.5 m, read at 20 m)
anchors.survey: GPS times of the point clouds of 24 tiles read: 2021-08-26 on tiles of the west and middle tongue, 2022-08-23 on the east tiles (GLAMOS names 20220823 for this surface). Tiles flown on both dates (no day with 85 % of the points) are not used.
anchors.placed_at: per tile: 2021-08-26 (48 % of ice cells, computed) or 2022-08-23 (41 %, computed)

anchors.survey: built from aerial images 2023: strips over the strip 2023-08-21 (CRYOSPHERE MONITORING, 78 % of ice cells, computed) and 2023-09-07 (SWISSIMAGE, covers every ice cell); GLAMOS names 20230823 (is-stand). Which strip fed which cell is not published.
anchors.placed_at: 2023-08-21 (tested: 10 Aug, 21 Aug, 31 Aug, 7 Sep, 20 Sep 2023; rmse 1.85, 1.94, 2.07, 2.19, 2.44 m; 21 Aug taken because a strip was flown that day, 10 Aug has none; chosen on the same shots as the check, so not independent)

shape: Between two anchors the surface follows the lowering of the ice by elevation band: from snow-off (1 May plus Bw/|Bs| x 153 d, melt uniform: ASSUMPTION) to 30 September. GLAMOS release 2025 has NO elevation-band balance for Gornergletscher (no B56-07 row in the elevation-bin file); the band balance of each year is a straight line in elevation fitted (computed here, area weighted, 2200 to 3600 m) to the bins of Findel, Adler, Aletsch, Rhone and Corbassiere. Only its shape over elevation and years is used; the size of the change comes from the surveys. 2026 has no GLAMOS balance yet: the line is estimated from Aletsch glacier-wide 2026 values read from the GLAMOS figure (+-100 mm w.e.). Beyond the last anchor (2024 to 2026) the cell scale of the last segment is kept, applied to the measured 2023 surface with its own detail: the change comes from the difference of the anchor surfaces smoothed over about 100 m (median of 5 cells of 20 m, then a light Gaussian), because the raw cell by cell difference carries the noise and crevasse detail of surveys of different vintage and made 2024 to 2026 rough (computed roughness (standard deviation of the 20 m Laplacian on the 2023 ice) of 2026: 15.8 m raw, 6.1 m smoothed; 2023: 6.0 m). For 2024 to 2026 the lowering also fades to zero over the last 80 m before the 2023 ice outline (distance from the outline, linear; a modelling choice, not a measured value), so that no wall grows between the thinning ice and the ground outside, which is held at its 2023 height. Every cell stays between its two anchors, or, outside them, within 2.5 times the lowering of its band (in m of ice) of the nearest anchor.

validation.icesat2: ICESat-2 ATL06 v007, 1905 shots on 2023 ice, July to October, slope under 20 degrees, in 10 granules: bias 0.83 m, rmse 1.94 m over all years (error = model minus shot; the A2 day was chosen on the same shots). Per year: 2020 1.92 m (215 shots); 2021 1.38 m (287 shots); 2022 1.88 m (319 shots); 2023 1.74 m (513 shots); 2024 2.09 m (128 shots); 2025 2.43 m (443 shots). Years without summer shots are not checked.
validation.datum: Heights are corrected with a plane fitted on 12336 shots on stable ground outside the ice (NMAD 1.05 m).
validation.not_checked: The split of the loss between years is an assumption (even melt from snow-off to 30 September, band balance borrowed from neighbouring glaciers). ICESat-2 scores the surface in the years with shots, not each year step. ASTER DEMs (AST14DEM) were checked against the model for 2016 to 2024 (see the chart; 2025 and 2026 have no usable scene), with a per-scene offset taken from stable rock; ASTER is rough (stable-terrain NMAD 9 to 15 m per scene), so only differences of a few metres per year mean something. No stake check is possible: GLAMOS has no point balance readings for Gornergletscher after 2008-04-23. No radar-speed check was made.

bed: Ice surfaces are not allowed below the bedrock: swissBEDROCK (swisstopo, 10 m; under glaciers swissALTI3D minus a modelled ice thickness, GLAMOS 2020) is the floor.
not_used: No airborne research DEMs for Gornergletscher were searched or used. Years before 2016 are not modelled: older pictures use the 2016 surface. The seasonal lake on the glacier (Gornersee) is not modelled.
licences: swisstopo open government data (swissALTI3D, swissSURFACE3D, image-strip footprints). GLAMOS balances and volume change: non-commercial (file headers). ICESat-2 (NASA, ATL06) and ASTER AST14DEM (NASA LP DAAC): used for checking only; the ASTER terms of use were not read. GLAMOS ice thickness release 2020 (radar beds, CC BY 4.0 per the landing page) and swissBEDROCK (swisstopo open government data): used for the ice bed checks.
caveat_2026: estimate: extrapolated like 2024-2025, with the 2026 balance estimated from the GLAMOS figure for Aletsch (Gorner has no 2026 balance): provisional; not checked (no summer ICESat-2 shots)

page.mapcap: The model area = the 3D strip (outlined in black), as set in the walkthrough. Blue: ice inside the 2023 outline, about 18.5 km² (computed, 20 m cells). Red dashed: every cell modelled as ice, including ground that was ice at the 2015 survey, about 20.8 km² (computed). The 1,905 ICESat-2 shots used for the checks are shown in the 3D viewer (last section). Pictures of years before 2016 use the 2016 surface.
page.stakeNone: no stake-year: the GLAMOS point mass balance of Gornergletscher (release 2025; annual, winter and intermediate files) has readings from 2003-10-03 to 2008-04-23 only, none in 2016 to 2026.
page.icesatSub: also fits the 2023 anchor day (not independent)
page.icesatNote: Also used to choose the 2023 anchor day, so not an independent check.
page.asterNote: For scale: each used scene has a stable-terrain NMAD of 9.3 to 14.7 m (computed), and on the ice next to the anchor date (2023-09-07) ASTER reads −4.0 m against the 2023 surface, so differences of a few metres are within ASTER's own scatter. rms = spread of the scene values of the year. Check only, not in the fit.

notes.uncertainty: Median over the ice of 2023, red whisker the 90th percentile (computed). Calibrated on the same ICESat-2 shots (anchor value = the 2023 rmse, 1.74 m, an upper value); where a year has shots it is not below their rmse. Years without shots (2016 to 2019) carry the anchor value only, a lower bound. 2026 has none: it is an estimate and its balance was read from the GLAMOS figure for Aletsch.
notes.independent: ICESat-2 also fitted the 2023 anchor day, so it is not independent. ASTER scenes are checks only (20 of 99 scenes usable; none for 2025 and 2026). There are no stakes for Gornergletscher after 2008. Click a year for the numbers.
notes.sharing: Solid: the loss between two surveys is shared over the years by an elevation-band balance borrowed from five other glaciers (computed; GLAMOS has none for Gornergletscher). Dashed: extrapolated beyond the last survey (2026 with an estimated balance). Not used: measured years.

page.viewerText: The yearly surfaces in 3D with a year slider, the same viewer as for Aletsch. Switch on ICESat-2 shots (what the model was checked against) and hover a shot for its values; the bed and uncertainty colours are in the Colour menu. There are no stake readings for Gornergletscher. About 8 MB, loaded when you press the button.

bed.lead: Three checks on Gornergletscher (all computed here, not source figures). The bed is the rock under the ice. "Radar bed" is the radar's own bed elevation (the survey surface minus the measured thickness, from the GLAMOS release); "model bed" is swissBEDROCK, which under glaciers is swissALTI3D minus a modelled GLAMOS ice thickness.
checks:
1 · Radar bed against model bed

At the 1,371 radar cells (20 m, median of the points in a cell), how far apart are the two beds?

Median −0.2 m over all cells, but it depends on the survey: +0.5 m (2008, 693 cells), −2.2 m (2004, 607 cells), −19.6 m (1994, 71 cells). Spread (standard deviation) 4.2 m in 2008, 11.9 m in 2004, 21.8 m in 1994; over all cells 80 % are within 10 m and 97 % within 30 m.

Reading: close for the dense 2008 survey (96 % of its cells within 10 m), but not a validation. The model was made from these same surveys, and at the survey lines its bed is the measured bed (Grab et al. 2021, where the survey surface agreed with a DEM). The older lines are further off.

2 · One survey against another

Where two surveys covered the same spot, how well do they repeat?

Only 21 spots (25 m cells) have two survey dates (1994 and 2004: 8, 1994 and 2008: 1, 2004 and 2008: 12). The beds implied by the two surveys differ by a median +16.5 m (later minus earlier) with a standard deviation of 31.9 m; 24 % agree within 10 m.

Reading: too few spots for more than a hint, and the dense 2008 survey has only 13 spots in common with another. Single radar cells can differ by tens of metres.

3 · Ground that is ice free now

Radar points where the newest swissALTI3D shows ground, not ice: the exposed ground is the bed.

490 points (488 from 2008, 2 from 2004), ice about 101 m thick:

2008
Radar bed − ground now−3.8 m (−5.1 to −2.5)
Model bed − ground now−4.6 m (−6.0 to −0.4)

Median, in brackets the middle half (the 2004 points are too few to show). 14 % of the points have the radar bed above the ground now.

bed.read:
What this supports

  • At the margins both beds lie a few metres below the exposed ground: the radar bed by 3.8 m, the model bed by 4.6 m (medians of the 2008 points). That is the opposite sign to Aletsch, where the radar bed lay above the ground.
  • So the two beds are close to each other here (less than 1 m apart in the medians) and both a few metres under the ground that is now ice free. Reasons were not tested (for example lowered ground, a position error, or the survey surface).

What it does not show

  • Very few places: the 490 points lie on 2 flight profiles, so the medians rest on two lines.
  • Not the deep tongue: these are margin points, about 101 m of ice; deeper ice may behave differently.
  • Not a model error band: the model's own uncertainty maps are not in the GLAMOS release, and swissBEDROCK's uncertainty band under glaciers is about 0 (not usable).
  • Not screened: lakes and debris on the exposed ground (the seasonal lake Gornersee lies on the glacier), and positions at the margin (a few metres of horizontal error).

How the ice-free points were chosen

  • In the 3D strip, at least 30 m outside the SGI2023 outline (acquired 2023, all glaciers) and at least 30 m inside the SGI2016 outline, so the model had ice there.
  • Newest swissALTI3D edition, ground slope at the point at most 20°. With up to 30°: 544 points, radar −3.8 m, model −4.6 m. With a 50 m margin: 288 points, radar −3.7 m, model −5.0 m; with 100 m none.
